profile.migration_strategy_justification: The immutable workflow pin becomes the only item behavior authority after the additive registry and pin backfill are applied, and the code-owned built-in revisions become the defaults for subsequent items.

invariants: The items row count is unchanged even when missing code-owned workflow revisions are appended.
Every item retains a complete immutable workflow pin and a stage accepted by that version.
Workflow pin columns are required, the superseded classification is absent, and item stages have no fixed database vocabulary.
Each built-in workflow selects the code-owned immutable revision for subsequently created items without repinning existing items.
attestation.residual_risk_notes: The migration takes an exclusive items-table lock, validates every immutable pin and stage before DDL, preserves the items row count, and may append one code-owned revision per built-in workflow before selecting it without changing existing item pins. Overall affected-table row counts are therefore intentionally not preserved. It remains deliberately merge-boundary breaking because older code still reads the superseded column.
